# Course authoring

Read the repository README, binding product specification and `docs/content/COURSE-AUTHORING-WORKFLOW.md`. Use the same blueprint, instructional contract, engine facts and compiler regardless of authoring provider.

Define a bounded competence graph before writing the catalog. Teach prerequisites before using them, map evidence to narrow shared KCs, and close every taught skill with later independent retrieval. A capstone applies several previously taught skills. Do not confuse a framework checklist with a teaching sequence or a numerical lesson target with mastery.

Include every required shared KC prerequisite explicitly. Additional course-specific preparation is allowed only when it is also taught earlier and matches the lesson contract. Do not turn the incidental order of one course into a universal prerequisite, or credit a broad computation skill for an exercise that only identifies a category.

Write explanations and plausible misconceptions before keys. Use engine interactions when they represent the concept. Check what the actual scorer verifies before praising an action. Recompute arithmetic from visible inputs; numeric proofs and model validation do not establish the correctness of financial assumptions or prose claims. Review each localization and complete screen load, not just individual strings.

Direct agents author the plan files without provider calls. Forge uses the same private authoring packet and validations; paid calls still require the task's spending authorization. Build the entire course with `course:build`, validate its emitted rows with Core, and inspect the actual lesson player. Do not bypass failures or erase review findings to meet a deadline.

Report authorship, technical verification, editorial review, novice evidence and production release separately. Synthetic capacity tests are not a catalog; successful compilation is not measured retention. Preserve the task's explicit scope and existing authorization. This skill adds no publication, spending or deletion permission.

## Calibration before mass generation

The current 36 Financial Education lessons are calibration material, not the production course. Keep their blueprint marked `publication_intent: calibration-only`; live publication and attestation must reject it. Use owner review and actual-player findings to improve shared authoring instructions, validators and regression cases, rather than only polishing those 36 files. After calibration, design a separate broad introductory financial curriculum of hundreds of coherent lessons, with explicit boundaries for specialist courses. Generate in bounded batches with the same instructional, mathematical, localization and player checks, then recheck cross-batch prerequisites, retrieval and duplication. Do not equate passing the calibration corpus with completion of that production curriculum.
